key_insight: Adding a branching degree-of-freedom structure to a shell-model cascade strengthens intermittency and produces more anomalous energy-transfer scaling than the standard single-branch Sabra model.
engineering_relevance: Reduced turbulence models should capture not only nonlinear triadic interactions but also the geometry of how modes proliferate across scales if they are to reproduce realistic intermittent cascade behavior.
method: Build a multi-branch shell model combining quasi-local triadic interactions with scale-dependent branching.
Compare cascade statistics against the standard Sabra shell model.
Use multiplier statistics and large-deviation analysis to quantify multiplicative cascade behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that branching increases intermittency, as shown by anomalous scaling exponents of energy-flux structure functions and by multiplier/large-deviation statistics.
watch_item: Because the study relies on reduced shell models, the conclusions may not transfer quantitatively to full Navier-Stokes turbulence without further validation.
paper_title: Intermittency in Shell Models of Turbulent Cascades: from Single-Branch to Multi-Branch
